steps.body: Measurement works the same way: a centimeter is a hundredth of a meter, so 74 cm is 0.74 m without any calculation beyond naming the place.
steps.narration: Measurement works the same way: a centimeter is a hundredth of a meter, so 74 cm is 0.74 m without any calculation beyond naming the place.

widget.prompt: How many centimeters in 3 meters? Hop one meter at a time.

commonLandings.feedback: Two hops reach 200 cm; the length is three meters.
Four hops overshoot — three meters is 300 centimeters.

widget.missFeedback: Each meter is 100 centimeters, so three reach 300.
widget.successFeedback: 300 — three hops of a hundred centimeters, which is why 3 m and 300 cm are the same length.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — each meter is 100 centimeters, so three reach 300.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — three meters stops exactly at 300 centimeters.

predict.prompt: 74 cm in meters — bigger or smaller number?
predict.reveal: Meters are larger units, so fewer of them cover the same ribbon and the number shrinks.

cml.actionGoal: Work in the smallest place the numbers use, then decide where the point belongs for g5dc measurement.
invariants: A decimal is place value continued past the ones: computing in the smallest shared place turns g5dc measurement into whole-number arithmetic, and the point's position records which place the digits landed in.
misconceptions: Right-aligning digits instead of the points, treating a trailing zero as a change in value, or losing count of the decimal places a product carries.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the point moved one place left, how many times smaller would the amount become?

widget.prompt: A ribbon measures 39 centimeters. One meter is 100 centimeters. Write the length in meters as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: 39 is the length in CENTIMETERS; meters are bigger, so the number must shrink.
That divided by ten. A meter holds one hundred centimeters, not ten.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Work in the smallest place the numbers use, then decide where the point belongs.
